key_insight: Reinforcement learning training makes classifier gradients unstable and small, disrupting gradient-based adversarial optimization and improving robustness when combined with adversarial training.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a practical hybrid defense for deployed vision models: use RL-induced gradient regularization to harden models against attacks that depend on accurate gradient signals.
method: Train image classifiers with policy-gradient objectives plus epsilon-greedy exploration
Analyze gradient behavior, loss landscapes, and predictive entropy to explain robustness
Combine RL with adversarial training (RL-adv) and compare against SL-adv
evidence_signal: Across CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and ImageNet-100, the study evaluates multiple architectures against PGD, AutoAttack, transfer-based, and query-based attacks, with RL-adv achieving the strongest robustness.
watch_item: RL training may add optimization complexity and can depend on attack settings and iteration budgets, so gains should be validated for the target deployment and threat model.
paper_title: Reinforcement Learning Disrupts Gradient-Based Adversarial Optimization
